## STEP 1 — PRE-COMMITMENT

My causal identification strategy is to estimate the return to schooling using a **within-identical-twin differences approach**, which acts as a robust control for unobserved genetic ability, shared family background, and common environmental factors that are constant within a twin pair. This eliminates key sources of omitted variable bias. To further address the issue of **measurement error in self-reported education**, which can attenuate OLS and within-twin OLS estimates, I will employ an **Instrumental Variable (IV) strategy**. Specifically, one twin's report of the other twin's education will serve as an instrument for the focal twin's self-reported education.

My directional hypothesis is that there is a **positive and statistically significant causal effect of schooling on hourly wages**.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Instrumental variables within identical twin pairs — within-pair education difference is used to identify returns to schooling (controlling for genetic and family background); co-twin's report of education serves as instrument for self-reported education (addressing measurement error attenuation bias)

key_variables.treatment: years of schooling (continuous, self-reported), instrumented by co-twin's report of the individual's education
key_variables.control: identical twin sibling (shares genes and family environment — within-pair differencing controls for ability and background)

_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The causal return to schooling is positive and significant. Within-twin IV estimates yield approximately 12-16% return per year of education, which is actually higher than OLS estimates (~8-10%). The higher IV estimate relative to OLS suggests that measurement error attenuation in self-reported education is a more important bias than ability bias (upward), consistent with the hypothesis that within-twin education differences are driven by random factors rather than ability differences.
_ground_truth.main_effect: IV within-twin return to education: approximately 12-16% per year; OLS within-twin: ~8-10%; cross-sectional OLS: ~10%
key_robustness: Within-twin fixed effects (differencing out shared family/genetic factors)
IV using co-twin's report as instrument for measurement error correction
Hausman test comparing OLS and IV estimates (testing for measurement error bias)
Separate estimates by sex (male vs. female twins)
Sensitivity to sample selection (Twinsburg festival attendees may not be representative)

identification_strategy_detail.method: Within-identical-twin differenced wage equation, with co-twin-reported education as IV for self-reported education
identification_strategy_detail.treatment: Years of education (continuous), with within-twin variation identifying the return; co-twin's report instruments for measurement error
identification_strategy_detail.unit_of_observation: Individual within an identical twin pair (approximately 680 individuals in 340 pairs)
identification_strategy_detail.key_assumption: Within identical twin pairs, differences in education are uncorrelated with differences in unobserved ability or earnings potential. This requires that whatever caused the twins to get different amounts of education (personal choices, luck, different peer groups) is not itself correlated with earnings. Co-twin's report of education is correlated with true education but measurement errors in co-twin reports are uncorrelated with errors in self-reports.

key_magnitudes.iv_return: 12-16% per year of education (within-twin IV, correcting for measurement error)
key_magnitudes.within_twin_ols: 8-10% per year (within-twin OLS, not corrected for measurement error)
key_magnitudes.measurement_error: Self-reported education has approximately 10-15% error rate, causing ~30-40% attenuation of within-twin OLS

_ground_truth.robustness_notes_detail: The finding that IV > OLS (within twins) is consistent with measurement error attenuation being a larger bias than ability bias in the within-twin design. Hausman tests reject the null that measurement error is negligible. Results are qualitatively similar for male and female twins. The Twinsburg Festival sample may not be representative of the U.S. population (twins who attend a festival may differ from the general twin population), but the within-twin design is internally valid regardless of external validity concerns.
